plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large, bright yellow flower head surrounded by ray petals and a dense central disc of tiny florets. The heads track the sun when young, and the plant is widely grown for seed, oil and ornament.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn in the Northern Hemisphere (July to September)
plants.location: Native to North America; widely cultivated in the United States, Ukraine, Russia, France and Argentina
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is not a single flower but a composite of up to 2,000 tiny florets, each of which can develop into a seed. The spiral arrangement of these florets follows Fibonacci numbers.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray narrow leaves and dense spikes of fragrant purple flowers. It thrives in sunny, well-drained soils and is a magnet for bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August)
plants.location: Native to the western Mediterranean; cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and its name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large round leaves held above the water and spectacular flowers on tall stalks. The leaves have a microscopic surface structure that repels water and dirt.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer, peaking July to August in temperate Asia
plants.location: Native to Asia and northern Australia; found in ponds and wetlands in India, China, Vietnam and Japan, and cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: Lotus seeds can remain viable for centuries; one seed about 1,300 years old was successfully germinated after being found in a dry lake bed in China.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A shrub bearing the largest flower head in the Protea genus, with a bowl of silky-tipped, colored bracts surrounding a center of tiny flowers. It is the national flower of South Africa.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering from about May to November and a peak around August
plants.location: Native to the fynbos of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa; grown in Australia, Hawaii and California
plants.funFact: Proteas are among the most ancient flowering plants, dating back around 300 million years, and they are adapted to fire, with some resprouting from underground tubers after wildfires.
